## Code quality checks

`crafter-lint` enforces these rules on every change. Each finding names the fix; apply it instead of raising a limit, adding a suppression or editing the baseline. Run `crafter-lint check --changed` before you finish; it only reports what your change touches. A function that was already over a limit is a note: restructure it in its own commit if the task covers it.

- **cognitive-complexity** (error): No function goes over the cognitive complexity max. Every branch and nesting level is context a reader holds at once; past the max, a function takes much longer to review and is easier to break.
- **max-nesting** (error): Control flow nests at most a few levels deep. Each level is a condition the reader must keep in mind; deep nesting is where off-by-one branches hide.
- **max-file-lines** (error): Files stay under a line limit (checked only when `max` is set). A file that fits in one read has one obvious home for each change.
- **no-silent-catch** (error): A catch block that does nothing says why, or surfaces the error. An empty catch turns a failure into silence: the bug ships and nobody sees it until a user does.
- **no-silent-promise-catch** (error): `.catch(() => {})` says why, or surfaces the error. A swallowed rejection is the async form of an empty catch: the operation fails and the UI keeps going as if it worked.
- **no-double-cast** (error): No `as unknown as T` without a SAFETY comment. A double cast turns off the type checker for that value; the next change to either type compiles and breaks at runtime.
- **no-non-null-assertion** (warn): No `value!` without a SAFETY comment. `!` asserts a value exists without checking; when it doesn't, the crash happens far from the cause.
- **no-ignored-hook-deps** (error): Hook dependencies are fixed, not ignored. Ignoring exhaustive-deps hides stale closures: the effect reads values from an old render.
- **no-narration-comment** (warn): Comments describe the code, not its history. History comments rot the moment the next change lands; git already records what changed and why.
- **no-duplicate-function** (warn): One implementation per behaviour: no copied function bodies across the repo. Two copies drift: the next fix lands in one and the bug survives in the other.
- **no-dead-export** (warn): Every export is imported somewhere. An export nobody imports is a public surface nobody uses: it misleads readers about what depends on it and keeps dead code alive.
- **layer-boundaries** (error): Layers import only the layers they are allowed to. A boundary that is only written down gets crossed by the first change in a hurry; a crossed boundary makes the lower layer impossible to change or delete on its own.
- **biome** (warn): The project's Biome lint diagnostics, in the same report and baseline (when `enabled`). One place to read every check means an agent cannot pass one tool and miss the other.
<!-- crafter-lint:end -->
